title: “One-Size-Fits-All”? Examining Expectations around What Constitute “Fair” or “Good” NLG System Behaviors
reasoning: The paper focuses on the sociolinguistic aspects of fairness in Natural Language Generation (NLG), specifically examining the tension between invariance and adaptation. While it touches upon 'fairness' and 'good' behaviors, it is an empirical study of human expectations and system behaviors regarding social identity features (names, roles, dialects) rather than a benchmark or evaluation of religion, morals, or specific ethical frameworks.
